name: Star Timer as Health Bar
description: The Baby-Mario star countdown becomes a health bar: taking damage drains it by a fixed amount (default 3 on-screen units) and it no longer refills. When it empties, Yoshi is killed outright - an explicit death-spike, the way the Flutter hack does it. Pair with "Fast Reset on Death" to make that an instant restart instead of the full death/retry. Add "Star Timer Damage Amount" to change the drain. Pair with "Disable Losing Baby Mario" as well: without it, every hit still floats Baby Mario off into a bubble (the vanilla recapture mechanic this health bar repurposes), so DLBM keeps Baby with Yoshi and makes the drained bar your only life meter. The two don't overlap - this patch's empty-bar kill is the generic death-spike DLBM doesn't touch.
attribution: Faithful to the Flutter hack (https://www.romhacking.net/hacks/8972/): a reducer drains and clamps the star timer, and a rewritten CODE_01C2AE death-spikes Yoshi the moment it empties.
details: Three edits, mirroring the Flutter hack (verified by disassembling it). (1) Drain on damage: a trampoline in player_hit (CODE_player_hit+$31 = $03:A884, replacing the hurt-sound load) jumps to StarTimerReducer (%patchcode, reserved $51 pool slice) which subtracts amount*10 from the star timer ($03B6, stored x10), clamps at 0, replays the hurt SFX, and resumes player_hit. Like Flutter's reducer at $A1:B46C it only CLAMPS - it does not kill. (Flutter's reducer indexes a per-enemy drain table at $A1:B4EA plus two boss special-cases, and drains from a second site at $05:A555; this port uses one flat amount from the single player_hit site, tunable via 'Star Timer Damage Amount'.) (2) No regeneration: forces the regen entry branch at CODE_00E2CC+$06 ($00:E2D2, BCS -> BRA) to always skip so the meter never refills (byte-identical to Flutter). (3) Kill when empty: Flutter rewrites CODE_01C2AE - the per-frame star-timer/HUD routine - to call the generic death-spike CODE_player_death_spike ($04:AC9C) the moment the timer drops below $0A (on-screen 0). This port hooks the head of CODE_01C2AE with a JML to StarTimerHealthKill (%patchcode), which - only in RUN_LEVEL (gm0F), and only when no death/transition is already running - checks $03B6 < $0A and if so does REP #$10 : JSL CODE_player_death_spike. death-spike is LDA #$0E : JSL CODE_04F6E2, i.e. it routes through exactly the routine 'Fast Reset on Death' hijacks - so an empty bar becomes an instant restart (with Fast Reset off it is a normal gm11 death). A $60AC (Player_CurrentState) == $0E re-trigger latch (restored from Flutter) fires the kill ONCE: death-spike does not change the game mode, so without Fast Reset the empty bar would otherwise re-spike every frame and freeze; the latch lets the normal spike-death run to completion. The stub does NOT write a death jingle (PlayMusic=$07): with Fast Reset on, the reload carries the level music through (upload_music_data early-returns instead of re-uploading), so a jingle would stop the song with nothing to restart it - the 'short riff then silence' bug (traced to the stub at $23E053). Flutter's C2AE doesn't write the jingle either; the reroute's SFX $22/$17 are the death cue and the level song never breaks. The stub then reproduces the 3 displaced gate instructions (LDA $0B4C : ORA $0B57 : ORA $0B59) and JMLs back to CODE_01C2AE+$09 so the rest of the routine runs unchanged. This replaces the earlier 'rely on stock lose-Baby-at-0' approach (which needed the hit to bubble Baby off and could race the knockback - the 'glitchy quick-reset' bug); vanilla C2AE does NOT in fact death-spike on its own, so the explicit hook is both more faithful to Flutter and more reliable. Composition: COMPOSES with "Disable Losing Baby Mario" (our DLBM is byte-identical to Flutter's 36 edits) - DLBM neutralizes the kidnap/swallow CINEMATIC actors, while this kill is the generic death-spike DLBM does not touch. "Star Timer Damage Amount" overrides the amount operand at StarTimerReducer+1 (label-resolved). All addresses are label-injected from the build .sym (drift-proof). The midring/empty-bar paths still want an in-game pass.
asm: ; --- Star Timer as Health Bar ---
; (1) no regeneration: force the regen entry branch to always skip
org !CODE_00E2CC+$06 : db $80                ; CODE_00E2CC: BCS -> BRA (the star meter never refills) [label-injected, drift-proof]
; (2) drain on damage: trampoline in player_hit -> reducer in the patch pool
org !CODE_player_hit+$31 : JML StarTimerReducer : db $EA,$EA,$EA   ; replaces the hurt-sound load in player_hit (JML 4b + 3 pad bytes)
; (3) FLUTTER-PARITY KILL: empty bar -> death. Flutter rewrites CODE_01C2AE to
;     call the generic death-spike the instant the star timer drops below 1.0; we
;     hook the head of CODE_01C2AE (the per-frame star-timer/HUD routine) and do the
;     same. death-spike routes through CODE_04F6E2 - the routine 'Fast Reset on Death'
;     hijacks - so an empty bar becomes an instant restart (a normal gm11 death if
;     Fast Reset is off). Replaces the old 'rely on stock lose-Baby-at-0' path, which
;     needed the hit to bubble Baby off and could race the knockback.
org !CODE_01C2AE : JML StarTimerHealthKill : db $EA,$EA,$EA,$EA,$EA   ; displace 'LDA $0B4C : ORA $0B57 : ORA $0B59' (9b); return to the BNE at +$09
; --- star-timer reducer (%patchcode: reserved $51 pool slice) ---
; Mirrors the Flutter hack's reducer ($A1:B46C): drain the star timer and
; CLAMP at 0 - it does NOT kill. The kill is the separate CODE_01C2AE hook (3)
; above, which death-spikes once the bar reads empty - exactly how Flutter splits
; it (reducer clamps; rewritten C2AE kills). NOTE: Flutter's reducer indexes a
; per-enemy drain table ($A1:B4EA) + boss cases and drains from a 2nd site
; ($05:A555); this port uses one flat amount from a single player_hit site.
%patchcode()
StarTimerReducer:
LDA.w #$0003                             ; drain amount (low byte = StarTimerReducer+1; override via 'Star Timer Damage Amount')
ASL A
STA.w $146E
ASL A
ASL A
CLC
ADC.w $146E
STA.w $146E                              ; amount * 10 (the star timer is stored x10)
LDA.w !RAM_YI_Level_StarTimerLo
SEC
SBC.w $146E
BPL .store                               ; result >= 0 -> keep it
LDA.w #$0000                             ; underflow -> clamp to 0 (the (3) CODE_01C2AE hook then death-spikes)
.store:
STA.w !RAM_YI_Level_StarTimerLo
JSL !CODE_push_sound_queue               ; replay the hurt SFX the trampoline overwrote [label-injected]
JML !CODE_player_hit+$38                 ; return into player_hit; the (3) C2AE hook kills next frame when the bar is empty
%endpatchcode()
; --- empty-bar kill (%patchcode): runs at the head of CODE_01C2AE every frame ---
; Flutter rewrites C2AE so the star timer dropping below $0A -> JSL death-spike,
; gated by a $60AC == $0E re-trigger latch ($60AC = Player_CurrentState, which
; death-spike's CODE_04F6E2 sets to $0E). We RESTORE that latch: death-spike does
; NOT change the game mode, so without 'Fast Reset on Death' the bar stays empty
; and this per-frame hook would re-spike every frame -> the death never advances
; -> freeze. The $60AC==$0E check makes it fire ONCE; the normal spike-death then
; runs to a gm11 death. With Fast Reset the reroute also swaps the game mode, so
; the gm0F guard skips too -> the two compose (fast reset on an empty bar).
%patchcode()
StarTimerHealthKill:
LDA.w !RAM_YI_Global_CurrentGameMode : CMP.w #$000F : BNE .resume  ; only in RUN_LEVEL (gm0F). With Fast Reset on, its reroute
;   swaps the mode to gm0B/gm35, so next frame this also skips.
LDA.w !RAM_YI_Level_DeathCurtainXPosLo : ORA.w $0B57 : ORA.w $0B59  ; a death curtain / screen transition already running?
BNE .resume                                  ;   yes -> skip (don't death-spike mid-transition)
LDA.w $60AC : CMP.w #$000E : BEQ .resume      ; FLUTTER re-trigger latch: Player_CurrentState already $0E
;   (TouchedSpike) => a spike-death is already underway. Fires the
;   kill ONCE so the standalone (no Fast Reset) death runs to
;   completion instead of re-spiking every frame (the freeze).
LDA.w !RAM_YI_Level_StarTimerLo : CMP.w #$000A  ; star timer is stored x10; < $0A => the on-screen bar reads 0
BCS .resume                                  ;   >= 1.0 -> bar not empty -> let CODE_01C2AE run normally
REP.b #$10                                    ; death-spike expects 16-bit X/Y. NOTE: deliberately NO PlayMusic=$07
;   death-jingle write here. Fast Reset's reload CARRIES the level music
;   through - upload_music_data early-returns (mirror still matches the
;   level header), it does NOT re-upload - so stopping the song with a
;   jingle leaves nothing to restart it: 'short riff then silence' (traced
;   to PC $23E053). Flutter's C2AE doesn't write the jingle either; the
;   reroute's SFX $22/$17 are the death cue and the level song never breaks.
JSL.l !CODE_player_death_spike                ; $04:AC9C = LDA #$0E : JSL CODE_04F6E2 (-> Fast Reset reroute) + death comms
SEP.b #$10
.resume:
LDA.w !RAM_YI_Level_DeathCurtainXPosLo : ORA.w $0B57 : ORA.w $0B59  ; reproduce the displaced gate so CODE_01C2AE's 'BNE +41' sees the right Z flag
JML.l !CODE_01C2AE+$09                         ; return into CODE_01C2AE at $01:C2B7
%endpatchcode()
